name: Antipas, Smyrna, and Philadelphia
charge: Faithful unto death; keeping the word of his patience; not denying his name in the place where Satan’s seat is
summary: To Smyrna Christ said he knew their works, tribulation, and poverty, and that they were rich, and told them to fear none of the things they were about to suffer, to be faithful even to death, and he would give them a crown of life (Revelation 2:8-10). At Pergamos, where Satan’s seat is, they held fast his name and had not denied his faith even in the days when Antipas his faithful martyr was slain among them (Revelation 2:12-13). Philadelphia had a little strength, kept his word, and had not denied his name, and an open door was set before it that no man can shut (Revelation 3:7-8).
offenseFull: To Smyrna he granted the works, the tribulation, and the poverty, and then said they were rich (Revelation 2:9). All the promises belonged to them whatever their purse held. In the same verse he named the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. The history identifies them: the house of Herod, Edomites converted in generations before and sitting in the congregations, which is how Drusilla the daughter of Herod Agrippa is called a Jewess, and how men brought up with Herod the tetrarch are found among the teachers at Antioch (Acts 13:1). Judah means the praise of the Lord, and Edom was never called that. Then the warning: fear none of those things they should suffer, for the devil would cast some of them into prison that they might be tried, and they would have tribulation ten days, and they were to be faithful even to death for a crown of life (Revelation 2:10). Christ had said the same: hands would be laid on them, they would be delivered to the synagogues and into prisons, and it would turn to them for a testimony (Luke 21:12-13); and they were not to fear them which kill the body but cannot kill the soul (Matthew 10:28). The trying is the point: then shall they be known who are my chosen, and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire (2 Esdras 16:73). He that endures to the end shall be saved (Matthew 10:22), and blessed is the man that endures temptation, for when he is tried he shall receive the crown of life (James 1:12).

At Pergamos the record names one man. Christ knew where they dwelt, where Satan’s seat is, and that they held fast his name and had not denied his faith even in the days when Antipas his faithful martyr was slain among them (Revelation 2:12-13). The account preserved of him is that John the apostle ordained him bishop of Pergamon, and that he was put to death under Nero for casting out the demons the local population worshipped, roasted inside a brazen bull shaped altar. It was not a quick death, and it came under the emperor known for burning our people alive. The city was given over to the same idolatry the apostles met at Lystra, where the people called Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercurius and brought oxen and garlands to sacrifice to them, and stoned Paul when he told them to turn from those vanities to the living God (Acts 14:11-19). The teaching draws the line hard: nobody threatens a man who goes along with what everybody else does. Antipas spoke against the worship of that city and they cooked him for it.
judgmentFull: To Smyrna: he that overcomes shall not be hurt of the second death (Revelation 2:11). The ones beheaded for the witness of Jesus and for the word of God, who had not worshipped the beast nor his image nor received his mark, live and reign with Christ, and on such the second death has no power (Revelation 20:4-6). That is what a crown of life is worth.

To Philadelphia, the city whose name means brotherly love, he writes as the one that is holy and true, that has the key of David, that opens and no man shuts (Revelation 3:7). That key is Isaiah’s, laid upon his shoulder (Isaiah 22:22), and it is the book sealed with seven seals that no man was found worthy to open until the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, prevailed to open it (Revelation 5:1-5), after which he opened the understanding of the disciples (Luke 24:44-45). So the open door set before them is the understanding itself, and no man can shut it, though the scribes and Pharisees shut up the kingdom of heaven against men (Revelation 3:8; Matthew 23:13). They had a little strength, kept his word, and did not deny his name. He promised to make them of the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet and know that he had loved them (Revelation 3:9), and because they kept the word of his patience, to keep them from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world (Revelation 3:10). The patience is the keeping of the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus (Revelation 14:12), the law kept as the apple of the eye (Proverbs 7:1-2), and the hour is the hour in which the judgment of Babylon comes and so great riches come to nothing (Revelation 18:10,17-19). He told them to hold fast what they had, that no man take their crown, and promised the overcomer would be made a pillar in the temple of his God and go no more out (Revelation 3:11-12).

text.text: And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive;
I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.

Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.
And it shall turn to you for a testimony.
And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.
And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.
And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write; These things saith he which hath the sharp sword with two edges;

I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan’s seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth.
And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.
And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.
Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people.
Which when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,

And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, which made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein:
Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.
Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
And with these sayings scarce restrained they the people, that they had not done sacrifice unto them.
And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.
He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.

And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.
Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.

And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;
And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals.
And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice, Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof?
And no man in heaven, nor in earth, neither under the earth, was able to open the book, neither to look thereon.
And I wept much, because no man was found worthy to open and to read the book, neither to look thereon.
And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.

And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.
Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures,
I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.
But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.
Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.
Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth.
Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.
My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee.
Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.
Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.
For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off,
And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city!

And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate.
Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.

Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name.
He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.
